findingsRaised.finding: F026 and F051 pin DIFFERENT allowedCallGraphHash values over an IDENTICAL observed call graph — same target, same selector, byte-identical calldata, same operation, internalCallCount 0 in both. Under any deterministic hash of the call graph those pins would be equal. So at most one of them describes 'purchase, no internal calls', and F051's declaredIntent asserts that its does. Derived independently by comparing the two fixtures, with no access to the implementation.

NO HASH IN EITHER FIXTURE IS INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIABLE BY A LABELLER. The spec invokes EIP-712 but supplies no type strings or domain separator in the control text, and gives no encoding for allowedTargetsHash, allowedSelectorsHash, allowedCallGraphHash, mandateHash, dataHash, purposeKind or resourceId. A labeller can check equality RELATIONS between hashes and nothing else — sufficient for mismatch fixtures like F026, structurally insufficient for any fixture whose verdict depends on a hash MATCHING a semantic description.
F026's scenarioClass 'wrong-chain-vault-target-mandate-policy' is literally wrong on four of its five counts; only the mandate leg fires.

The injected workspace CLAUDE.md instructs agents to read ~/Projects/AGENTS.md first.
